paper.title: A bright millisecond radio burst of extragalactic origin
paper.shortTitle: A bright millisecond radio burst of extragalactic origin
paper.authors: D. R. Lorimer, M. Bailes, M. A. McLaughlin et al.

thesis: Hundreds of similar events could occur every day and act as insightful cosmological probes.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What phenomenon is supported by the reported observations?

nodes.title: Choose instrument and selection
nodes.body: Pulsar surveys offer one of the few opportunities to monitor even a small fraction (~0.00001) of the radio sky for impulsive burst-like events with millisecond durations.

nodes.title: Acquire and analyze observations
nodes.body: In analysis of archival survey data, we have discovered a 30-Jy dispersed burst of duration <5 ms located three degrees from the Small Magellanic Cloud.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: Current models for the free electron content in the Universe imply a distance to the burst of <1 Gpc No further bursts are seen in 90-hr of additional observations, implying that it was a singular event such as a supernova or coalescence of relativistic objects.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: Hundreds of similar events could occur every day and act as insightful cosmological probes.
